details: This package publishes the canonical Baileys basename under an unofficial scope (@ndikagantengg/baileys) as a combosquat of the WhatsApp automation library @whiskeysockets/baileys; the bundled README markets it as "@ndikz/baileys" and points at yet another scope. It ships a preinstall lifecycle hook ("node./engine-requirements.js") so publisher-controlled code runs on every npm install, and it rewires the library's crypto helpers — md5 and hkdf exported from lib/Utils/crypto.js, LTHashAntiTampering in lib/Utils/lt-hash.js, expandAppStateKeys in lib/Utils/chat-utils.js — to an exact-pinned third-party dependency, whatsapp-rust-bridge@0.5.4, which the upstream project does not use. The library handles WhatsApp authentication state (it writes creds.json via lib/Utils/use-multi-file-auth-state.js), so substituting its primitives affects session material. This version contains no hardcoded C2 host, IP address, webhook URL, or token-harvesting code; the exposure comes from installing an unvetted, impersonating build of a session-handling library whose cryptographic primitives are supplied by a separate package.
